candidate.answerReason: Central symmetry relates two figures under a half-turn; a centrally symmetric figure maps to itself under a half-turn. This is the distinction stated in A.

methods.label: Compare the two definitions
methods.explanation: Central symmetry describes two figures that coincide with each other after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about a point. A centrally symmetric figure coincides with itself after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about a point.
methods.levelReason: The distinction is explicitly part of the Grade 9 central-symmetry concept.
